name: USGS 2012 outer Estero Bay multibeam depth and sounding-spread grids

producer.name: U.S. Geological Survey Pacific Coastal and Marine Science Center

units.within_cell_sounding_standard_deviation: m in separate WGS84 G1150 grid

rights.license: USGS public-domain work; source metadata requires attribution and says not for navigation

spatial.horizontal_crs: NAD83(CORS96) UTM zone 10 for NAVD88 depth; WGS84(G1150) UTM zone 10 for sounding spread
spatial.vertical_datum: NAVD88 Geoid12 for the NAD83 bathymetry grid

temporal.update_cadence: Static survey; monthly source-integrity check after spatial audit

provenance.access_service: Original USGS Open-File Report 2013-1225 ZIP and FGDC metadata
transformations: Inspected native ESRI ASCII header: 11,456 columns, 16,020 rows, 2 m cell size; source states mixed 2 m/4 m survey data, resampled into a 2 m mosaic.
No NAVD88-to-MLLW transformation or fishing target has been approved.

evidence.supports: 117 survey lines, about 165 square kilometres of outer Estero Bay, 45–250 m below NAVD88; the report compares a 1.96-times-sounding-spread TVU estimate with IHO standards.
The processing report documents NAD83(CORS96)/NAVD88 Geoid12, estimated sounding TPU, 2 m cells under 100 m, and 4 m data beyond 100 m resampled into the final mosaic.
Original NAD83/NAVD88 bathymetry and separate WGS84 sounding-standard-deviation archives are publicly listed.
Original source metadata gives the bounding box, collection dates, source restrictions and 2 m output grid.

limitations: The source's sounding standard deviation is a precision or terrain-variation statistic, not by itself a total propagated product-uncertainty bound; the report warns that high-relief cells may reflect natural bottom variation.
Depth and spread grids use different horizontal realizations and shifted raster origins. Their rows cannot be paired by index without reviewed coordinate transformation and registration uncertainty.
NAVD88 depths require a reviewed spatial VDatum transformation to MLLW plus total vertical uncertainty before applying the 300 ft fishing limit.
The raster envelope contains nodata and includes 4 m native-depth data resampled onto a 2 m output grid beyond 100 m. It is not a navigation product or a set of fishing spots.
Overlap with independently classified seabed, biological observations, current MPAs, chart dangers and usable drift/route geometry remains unreviewed.
